mechanism_narrative: Sustained elevation in PARKS mobility (t-1w: +38.0%) signals outdoor activity preference that crowds out indoor retail-and-recreation visits. This substitution effect persists over the next four weeks, depressing RETAIL_REC relative to the baseline period.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS elevated at +38.0% in t-1w, +20.1% in t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days increases relative to the prior 28-day mean despite PARKS remaining above +15% for at least three of the four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Declining TRANSIT mobility (t-0w: -34.3%) indicates reduced commuting and inter-area travel. This suppresses spontaneous retail visits by workers and cross-district shoppers, driving RETAIL_REC downward over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT remains severely depressed at -34.3% in t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days while TRANSIT remains below -30% for all four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES mobility falls below -32% and RESIDENTIAL mobility remains elevated above +7%, household members substitute home-based leisure for retail visits. This dual condition triggers a four-week depression in RETAIL_REC.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES at -32.0% in t-0w, RESIDENTIAL at +7.3% in t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days while both WORKPLACES remains below -32% and RESIDENTIAL remains above +7% for at least three consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility stabilization near baseline (t-0w: -2.4%) signals restored confidence in essential shopping. This confidence spillover increases discretionary retail visits within one to two weeks as consumers resume normal shopping patterns.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM crosses above -5% and remains there for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over weeks 1-2 of the forecast period despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining above -5%.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-September marks the onset of autumn school term and back-to-work normalization in London. This seasonal shift drives WORKPLACES recovery and increases family retail visits (clothing, supplies) over the next four weeks, lifting RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises week-on-week by at least 3 percentage points in the first two weeks of the forecast
evidence_refs: fact:Decision date is 2021-09-15, coinciding with UK autumn term start
failure_condition: WORKPLACES fails to rise by 3+ points in either of the first two forecast weeks, and RETAIL_REC does not increase relative to the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent TRANSIT depression (t-0w: -34.3%) combined with WORKPLACES weakness (t-0w: -32.0%) indicates ongoing mobility restrictions or voluntary avoidance. If both remain suppressed, retail footfall will remain depressed over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT < -30% AND WORKPLACES < -30% for at least two consecutive weeks in the forecast period
evidence_refs: fact:Both series remain severely depressed in t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days while both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain below -30% for two or more consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility surge (t-1w: +38.0%) reflects weekend and leisure-time outdoor preference. If PARKS remains elevated above +25% into the forecast period, this sustained outdoor substitution will suppress indoor RETAIL_REC visits within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS > +25% in the first week of the forecast period
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at +38.0% in t-1w, indicating strong outdoor preference
regime_hint: fair weather or seasonal outdoor activity peak
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases in week 1 of the forecast despite PARKS exceeding +25%.

mechanism_narrative: Convergence of GROCERY_PHARM recovery (t-0w: -2.4%) and PARKS normalization (t-0w: +20.1%) signals consumer confidence stabilization. This dual signal triggers a shift from outdoor leisure back to indoor retail within two weeks, raising RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM > -5% AND PARKS declines by 10+ points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM at -2.4%, PARKS at +20.1% in t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over weeks 1-2 of the forecast despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining above -5% and PARKS declining by 10+ points.
